summary: Launch-readiness QA sweep focused on the two reported bugs. BUG A (panel switcher first-click nav) is NOT REPRODUCIBLE in preview — verified as admin (all 4 panels) and customer (allowed panel + Forbidden403 for disallowed panels): every panel navigates on the FIRST click. BUG B (storefront image save 413) is VERIFIED FIXED — as a fresh restaurant merchant, uploaded a 3000x2000 ~4.5MB cover, ~5.4MB logo, and 3 large gallery photos, clicked Save → PUT /api/merchant/storefront returned 200, toast 'Storefront saved', and after full page reload cover/logo/3 gallery images all persist (client-side fileToConstrainedDataURL correctly shrinks each base64 under the 1.35M-char cap so the 1.5M server limit is never hit).

issues: Top-right role chip still says 'Customer' with the customer icon even though the logged-in user is now user_type=restaurant (see screenshot). Cosmetic but confusing — the header role selector should reflect the current user_type after re-login.

action_items: BUG A (panel switcher first-click): NOT reproducible against current preview code (SubAppsDropdown.pick → setOpen(false)+navigate(route) works reliably). If the owner is still seeing this on the Play Store build, it's likely a stale Capacitor bundle — bump the WebView cache/version and re-publish. No frontend code change needed here.
BUG B (storefront 413): confirmed fixed by client-side constrained compression; nothing more to do.
Optional polish: keep the role chip in the top-right header in sync with user.user_type (currently shows 'Customer' for a restaurant merchant on /merchant/storefront).
critical_code_review_comments: SubAppsDropdown.pick() calls setOpen(false)+navigate() on the same tick — this is fine for react-router-dom v6 (navigate is synchronous). No race with useEffect cleanup. No changes required.

ProtectedRoute correctly shows a spinner while AuthContext.loading=true, then either renders Forbidden403 or the target page. It does NOT redirect to /login on wrong role (only on missing user), so a first-click Forbidden panel cannot inadvertently bounce through login and lose the intended route. Good.

MerchantStorefrontEditor.save posts { logo, cover, bio, gallery } as base64 strings. Payload can still be ~4-6MB total (4 images * ~1.35M chars). Consider adding a per-request timeout and streaming/multipart upload longer-term to reduce memory pressure, but not a launch blocker.

imageUtils.fileToConstrainedDataURL: 6-pass loop over quality [0.82..0.4] then dim*=0.8 is deterministic and terminates. Good; but note the last-resort branch at line 50 (`resolve(render(dim, 0.4))`) can still exceed maxChars for extreme inputs — a defensive reject or a hard minimum dim floor + toast would be safer.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Panel switcher on web preview navigates correctly on first click for anonymous, customer and admin users. Forbidden panels render Forbidden403 ('Access restricted') on first click; no redirect to /login. Storefront image save works with client-side fileToConstrainedDataURL (imageUtils.js) capping base64 at 1.35M chars — server limit MAX_STOREFRONT_IMG_LEN=1_500_000 is safely never breached. Reported behaviour on production (Capacitor Play Store) may be a stale bundle rather than a code bug.
rca of the issue: BUG A RCA: The reported symptom (first click doesn't navigate; second click after visiting Dashboard does) cannot be reproduced against the current preview build. SubAppsDropdown.pick calls setOpen(false)+navigate(route) synchronously; ProtectedRoute never redirects a mis-role click through /login (it renders Forbidden403 directly). Given the report is from the Play Store (Capacitor WebView), the most likely cause is a stale JS bundle cached by the WebView — the older SubAppsDropdown may have had setOpen inside a useEffect or an intermediate state that swallowed the first click. Recommend the owner bump the app version / cache-bust the WebView and re-publish. BUG B RCA (confirmed fixed): previously the raw FileReader result (~5MB base64) exceeded MAX_STOREFRONT_IMG_LEN=1_500_000, so PUT /api/merchant/storefront returned 413. Fix: imageUtils.fileToConstrainedDataURL iterates quality then dimensions until base64 length <=1.35M chars per image. Verified end-to-end: 4.5MB+ input JPEGs saved successfully, persisted after reload.
